svg.title: Poisoned Source APT29 watering holes kill chain
svg.desc: Single-lane chain of six stages: APT29-linked staging infrastructure registered from April 2026; three delivery vectors (compromised legitimate sites, AiTM lookalike sites, and the Plerdy SEO Tracker supply-chain script between 2026-08-27 and 2026-09-03); device fingerprinting that withholds payloads from non-touch and non-phone clients; three n-day exploit chains for iOS 16.7, iOS 18.5 and Android Chrome 139-145; cookie and device data exfiltration to ad.starx-net.com port 8881; and response break points. Critical stages are delivery and exploitation. Detection anchors are the five core domains, port 8881, the temfp.js loader path and the Plerdy main.js to edge-ord loader sequence.
svg.text: Poisoned Source: APT29 watering holes deliver iOS and Android n-day exploits
Vendor: Sekoia (2026-11-04) · Date: 2026-11-08 · Cluster: APT29 (moderate to high) · Day 138
WATERING HOLE + SUPPLY CHAIN LANE
Staging: lookalike and delivery domains registered Apr-Aug 2026, spread over several hosters [T1583.001 T1584]
flux-telemetry.com (2026-04-02), starx-net.com (04-03), america250.holiday (05-19), theowo.club (06-18), clouds-stacks.com
(08-26): per Sekoia, partly summarised | Hosting spread over AS395092 Shock Hosting, AS219399 servinga, AS9009 and AS57169
EDIS; Sekoia sees this as consistent with past APT29 practice
static.flux-telemetry.com ad.starx-net.com edge-ord.clouds-stacks.com
Delivery: 3 vectors - hacked sites, AiTM lookalikes, Plerdy SEO Tracker script [T1189 T1195.002 T1608.004]
Injected window.onload loader fetches /module/5b4c8fea5cbcee273e8d830f52-temfp.js; victims: UA gas producer, US chemical
trade body, CZ party, BG military site | Plerdy a.plerdy.com/public/js/click/main.js had code appended 2026-08-27 to
2026-09-03 that loads edge-ord.clouds-stacks.com; lookalikes: america250.holiday
a.plerdy.com/public/js/click/main.js -> edge-ord.clouds-stacks.com/module/...-temfp.js
Fingerprint and gate: 61 collectors POSTed, empty answer for non-phone or non-touch clients [T1059.007 T1592]
UltimateFingerprinter is about 2.3 MB, about 98% dead AngularJS; JSON POST to static.flux-telemetry.com/api/<nonce>/v1; the
reply text is executed as script | Class A filters iOS 16.7; Class C serves Chrome 139-145 except 143 and stops on SM-S938B;
Sekoia saw no other gate and no reuse of the fingerprint data
POST /api/uGmlx2pmMHU1jq7wZU2QWgeC28vbXalf/v1 (published nonce)
Exploitation: n-day chains A iOS 16.7, B iOS 18.5 DarkSword, C Android Chrome [T1203 T1068 T1211]
2025-43520; stages /v1 /v2 /v3 | C: CVE-2026-3910 renderer RCE + CVE-2025-27038 Adreno sandbox escape, then AndroSnitch
(libexploit.so); all flaws were patched before the campaign
ad.starx-net.com/api/<NONCE>/v1 /v2 /v3
Collection and exfiltration: cookies (A, C), full device data (B), Wi-Fi keys [T1539 T1005 T1041 T1571]
A: Safari Cookies.binarycookies as JSON to ad.starx-net.com:8881/telemetry/v12; B: sms.db, Mail, WhatsApp, Telegram,
Keychain, photos; C: Chrome Cookies, Login Data, WifiConfigStore.xml | Replay guard cookie VDGH_TOKEN_REF in A and B; Class
C has no replay guard (Sekoia); attribution to APT29 is moderate to high confidence, not proof
ad.starx-net.com:8881/telemetry/v12
Response and break points [no technique]
Patch iOS and Chrome; block the five domains and port 8881; remove or pin the Plerdy tag with SRI and CSP; reset sessions of
anyone who visited in the window | Rotate cookies and tokens, Wi-Fi keys and Keychain secrets of exposed phones; Lockdown
Mode for high-risk users; indicators decay, re-validate before blocking
SRI + CSP script-src + MDM patch floor
Detection anchors
Sigma 01-03, KQL k1-k3, YARA (2 rules), Suricata sids 9960001-9960003, PEAK H1-H3. Derived from the Sekoia report; no first-hand sample analysis.
Break points: patch floor, SRI and CSP on third-party tags, block 5 domains and port 8881, session reset for exposed users, Lockdown Mode.
